methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements. For the original research topic, the code comments and module description were parsed to extract key functionalities and constraints. For the generated technical specification, each section (header, combinational logic function, enhanced combinational description, interface behavior, timing dependency, and timing logic) was analyzed to identify distinct atomic units of information. Special attention was paid to boundary conditions, data loading mechanisms, and the Rule 90 update logic.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Next state of each cell is the XOR of its two neighbors
When `load` is asserted, cells are initialized with `data`
On each rising edge of `clk`, cells update their state according to Rule 90 when `load` is not asserted
Neighbors of q[0] and q[511] are always 0
Next state of q[0] is 0 XOR q[1]
Next state of q[511] is q[510] XOR 0
spec_atomic_units: Implements a 512-cell Rule 90 cellular automaton
Module has a clock input `clk`
Module has a load signal `load`
Module has a 512-bit data input `data`
Module has a 512-bit output `q`
When `load` is asserted, cells are initialized with `data`
On each rising edge of `clk`, cells update their state according to Rule 90 when `load` is not asserted
Next state of each cell `q[i]` is determined by the XOR of its left and right neighbors: `q[i-1]` and `q[i+1]`
Neighbors of q[-1] and q[512] are always zero
Combinational logic for cell `q[0]` is `0 ^ q[1]` which simplifies to `q[1]`
Combinational logic for cell `q[511]` is `q[510] ^ 0` which simplifies to `q[510]`
For all other cells `q[i]` (where 0 < i < 511), the combinational logic is `q[i-1] ^ q[i+1]`
Data input is loaded into the q register when the load input is high
Load operation happens synchronously with the rising edge of the clk signal
When load is low, on each rising edge of clk, the q register updates its value based on the Rule 90 calculation using the previous value of q
The critical path involves the Rule 90 calculation
The propagation delay through the XOR gates and the setup time of the `q` register determine the minimum clock period
The registers are updated on the positive edge of the `clk` signal
When `load` is high, `q` is loaded with `data`
When `load` is low, `q` is updated with the Rule 90 calculation (q[i] <= q[i-1] ^ q[i+1])
